question: A 70-year-old Caucasian male visits your office regularly for treatment of New York Heart association class IV congestive heart failure. Which of the following medications would you add to this man's drug regimen in order to improve his overall survival?
analysis: In patients with New York Heart Association class IV congestive heart failure, adding spironolactone has been shown to improve overall survival by reducing mortality rates and hospitalizations. Spironolactone is a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist that helps in managing fluid retention and reducing the strain on the heart.
